statement: A top-10 economy legally authorises fully automated decisions (no human sign-off) in a new benefits, tax or immigration domain (Official gazette; OECD.AI; by 2028-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: No qualifying authorisation identified in 2023. The in-phase direction of travel was toward more safeguards: a Bloc A draft government-wide policy presumed AI used in federal benefits and immigration to be rights-impacting with mandatory safeguards; a large economic bloc's provisional AI law added high-risk obligations; and a national inquiry into an automated debt-recovery scheme (non-top-10 economy) recommended review rights and auditing of automated decision-making. Bloc B gazettes not searched in this run.

items.summary: Bloc A's budget office released draft guidance for agency AI use that presumes uses in federal benefits, immigration, health, employment and law enforcement to be rights- or safety-impacting and mandates safeguards (impact assessments, real-world testing, monitoring, notice and remedy).
items.detail: Bloc A OMB, 'OMB Releases Implementation Guidance Following President Biden's Executive Order on Artificial Intelligence', 2023-11-01, draft memo 'Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use of Artificial Intelligence' for public comment (verified via web_extract this run). Draft only in-phase (finalised as M-24-10 in 2024, excluded).

items.summary: A major economic bloc's legislators reached a provisional deal on a comprehensive AI law: high-risk systems face obligations including a mandatory fundamental-rights impact assessment; citizens get a right to complaints and explanations of high-risk AI decisions affecting them. Not yet formally adopted.
items.detail: Bloc C Parliament press release 20231206IPR15699, 'Artificial Intelligence Act: deal on comprehensive rules for trustworthy AI', 2023-12-09 (verified via web_extract this run). The Bloc C is not itself a single top-10 economy, but binds several (Bloc D, Bloc E, Bloc F).

items.summary: A national royal commission into an automated welfare debt-recovery scheme reported 57 recommendations, including that where automated decision-making is used there be a clear review path, public explanation, published business rules, and a body to monitor and audit automated decisions.
items.detail: Report of the Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme (Bloc W), presented and tabled 2023-07-07, updated 2023-07-11; Recommendations 17.1-17.2 (verified via web_extract this run). Bloc W is outside the top-10 economies; context for backlash against fully automated benefits decisions.
